comparisonMethod: All 90 N07 questions are bound to exact frozen inputs and their accepted answers resolved by answer.optionId. I compared their primary actions across the five unit objectives and screened each prompt/key against all 945 accepted questions. Text similarity only located candidate overlaps; the exact whole objects for likely pairs were then read and compared for prompt facts, keyed action, unit objective, and decisive alternatives. Whole-object hashes use producer canonicalJson from patternly-content/scripts/build.mjs.

crossUnitFindings.assessment: This is a close reinforcement of accepted N02 B05 i028: both ask learners to retain exact immutable dataset/code revision identifiers for a published result, and both keys express that same underlying provenance invariant. N07 frames the decision at the serialized-snapshot boundary, which aligns it with the N07-B05 serialization/versioning objective; the prompt’s no-schema-evolution fact removes a migration distractor but does not create a new primary concept. The overlap can prime recall of the earlier answer and lowers the incremental decision value, so it is recorded as a nonblocking near-duplicate warning. The current question remains a valid application of the serialization-boundary objective; the contract does not require every question to introduce a unique concept or scenario.
crossUnitFindings.correction: No correction is required for this bounded review. For future curriculum revisions, an optional way to increase transfer value would be to make the serialized representation boundary decisive (for example, distinguish embedded immutable revision references from mutable labels in the stored snapshot) while retaining the existing supported provenance intent. Do not change the accepted N02 item or require a new N07 identity solely for variety.
crossUnitFindings.currentAcceptedOptionText: Store immutable dataset and code revision IDs with the published result snapshot.
crossUnitFindings.acceptedOptionText: Persist exact immutable dataset/code revision references on the audit-retained result; do not resolve “current” inputs later.
crossUnitFindings.currentPrompt: The notebook publishes a result together with the exact input dataset revision and analysis-code revision that produced it. Those revisions are immutable, and reviewers later rerun the same result. No schema change or old-reader migration is requested. What should the serialized snapshot retain?
crossUnitFindings.acceptedPrompt: In a research-notebook platform, the experiment owner must publish a result snapshot. Published outputs reference immutable inputs and code versions. A published run is retained for audit after current inputs change; it must point to the exact dataset and code revisions used. How should the published result retain provenance?

crossUnitFindings.assessment: Both mention exact exercise and scoring-policy revisions. N01 asks what defines the completion association. N07 asks what belongs in the completion commit and adds independently mutable profile state and an asynchronously rebuilt history projection; its alternatives and boundary explanation test whether those separate states belong in the completion transaction. This is a transaction-scope decision within B02, not simply another request to store the same references. The shared answer supports legitimate cross-unit reinforcement.
crossUnitFindings.currentAcceptedOptionText: Commit the completion with its exercise and scoring-policy revisions.
crossUnitFindings.acceptedOptionText: Reference the exact exercise revision and scoring-policy version from completion, despite later reuse of the title.
crossUnitFindings.currentPrompt: A practice tracker records a learner’s completed exercise. The completion must retain the exact exercise and scoring-policy revisions used; the learner’s current profile can change independently. A history projection is rebuilt asynchronously. Which state should the completion commit?
crossUnitFindings.acceptedPrompt: A practice tracker stores each published exercise revision by ID. Each completion points to that revision and the scoring-policy version used at the time; two revisions may display the same title. What should define a completed exercise’s association?

crossUnitFindings.assessment: Both use corrected invoices and a new issue linked to the rejected issue. N02 asks how retry identity differs from corrected-reissue identity. N07 provides an immutable serialized-exchange requirement and asks how to preserve exactly what auditors may later read; overwrite/rebuild alternatives fail that historical-representation requirement. The business case is close, but the immutable serialized-history boundary adds a distinct decision, so this is valid transfer practice rather than the same learner action.
crossUnitFindings.currentAcceptedOptionText: Append a new immutable issue and link it to the rejected issue.
crossUnitFindings.acceptedOptionText: Retry uses the existing issue ID; corrected reissue is a new issue record with a new ID and a link to the rejected one.
crossUnitFindings.currentPrompt: An invoice issue is serialized as an immutable exchange record. A corrected invoice must point to the rejected issue, and auditors may later read either issue exactly as it was sent. Which persistence shape preserves that history?
crossUnitFindings.acceptedPrompt: In a digital invoice exchange, the billing operator must reissue a rejected invoice. The new issue is traceable and does not double-charge the customer. Each invoice issue has an issue ID. Delivery retry repeats that issue ID; a corrected reissue gets a new issue ID and points to the rejected issue. How should the service distinguish retry from reissue?

withinN07Patterns.distinction: The recurring whiteboard story tests repository access, committed event cutoff, row-to-event mapping, and unit-of-work close before export. Those are separate layer decisions.
The backordered-request story tests collection access, parent/child split transaction, and persistence mapping. Shared identity/promise facts are relevant to distinct decisions.
The badge/revocation story tests consistency scope, column mapping, identity across loads, and serialized policy revision. The keyed actions differ by unit.
The invoice cluster spans mapping, local save ordering, immutable serialized history, and retry-versus-reissue identity. B05 i015 is assessed separately; no general same-story prohibition is applied.

qualityDisposition.confirmedIssue: No blocking cross-unit defect was confirmed in this B01–B05 slice. N07 B05 i012 is a close reinforcement of accepted N02 B05 i028: the keyed provenance action is nearly the same, so it carries a nonblocking answer-priming/redundancy warning. Its explicit serialized-snapshot framing fits the N07-B05 objective, and neither the spec nor contract requires unique concepts or scenarios.
qualityDisposition.legitimateReinforcement: N07 B02 i017 and N07 B05 i015 share facts/answer concepts with accepted questions but add distinct transaction-scope and serialized-history decisions respectively. Repeated scenario nouns or principles alone are not defects.
qualityDisposition.noQuota: No unique-concept, unique-scenario, length, or option-count quota is applied.

nonBlockingWarning.risk: The shared notebook/published-result facts and same exact-revision action may let a learner recall the earlier provenance answer, reducing this item’s incremental decision value.
nonBlockingWarning.disposition: Accepted as reinforcement at a different representation boundary: N02 asks for provenance on an audit-retained result; N07 asks what the serialized snapshot must retain. This is a quality warning, not a failure under the existing contract.
